strengths: The numbers a sentence states are mostly filled from the rule: `fillProse` and `PROSE_NUMBERS` (config.mjs:2999-3044) put a Call's cost, damage, progress, drain, turns and the finishing blow's multiplier into the text, so the Despair and Hope Call tiles, Strike, Pin and the Finishing Blow cannot drift from their tables. A script over the 553 config prose strings found every placeholder the English carries in its Polish twin too (0 mismatches).

Every config prose string has a Polish twin in lang/pl.json (553/553 by the same script, which is what `node tools/check.mjs prose` holds), and the 53 identical ones are glossary names kept English on purpose (Truth Bullet, the Remnant kinds, Call names).

Every export is in the `DRPG` aggregate (107 exports, 106 in the aggregate plus `DRPG` itself; R1233), and every TIMING, TRIAL and FACILITIES key but one (FACILITIES.timedUntil) has a reader outside the file.

The rules' numbers agree with both handbooks wherever I compared them: the Search, Observe, Analyze, Listen, Project, Sabotage, Dash, Shut, Force, Pick, Keep Watch, Palm and Frisk thresholds; the 16 Despair Calls' and 10 Hope Call tiles' prices; the Overflow's 20, its range 6-60 and its 13 darkenings; the opening rolls (8 and 20, the Key Remnant scale 5/4/3); the eleven crisis thresholds; Tamper's 9/12/15/18 ladder, the floor of 8, the fresh scene's 3, the trail's 15 and the body's 16.

The comments that record a measurement carry it and check out when recomputed: the Monocub first tier 11 (104 of 144 throws of 2d12, 72.2%; config.mjs:3531-3533), the Palm steal at 10 (77.8%) against a Search Tier 1 at 12 (65.3%) (1805-1807), the victim's opening at 20 with no Night disadvantage (16.7%; 3739-3742).
The defensive `callsGm` predicates (config.mjs:1963-1994) never throw into the sheet's render, and answer the safe stripe on an unknown world.

TABLE_NAME_WORDS and TABLE_COPY_WORDS (817-860) freeze the English before i18n.mjs rewrites the tables in place, so a Polish GM no longer writes a second set of table names or descriptions into a shared world.

findings.title: A Cleaning Tool's hint, and the player handbook, promise its tier off a Misleading Trail's 15; the GM scores the trail at 15 whatever the tool
findings.where: scripts/config.mjs:691 (ITEM_CATEGORIES.cleaningTool.hint) and 4537-4544 (the CLEANUP note); docs/handbooks/player-handbook.en.md:623 (Holding ready); scripts/cleanup.mjs:1666-1671 and 1791-1794
findings.what_happens: The item hint a player reads on every Cleaning Tool says "advantage on every clean-up roll but Move the Body, and its tier off the number to beat", and the player handbook says a Cleaning Tool in hand gives advantage and takes its tier off the threshold for a clean-up, except Move the Body. The code splits it the other way for the trail: attemptStageSix arms the tool's advantage for every key but moveBody, and resolveStageSix takes a tier off only where the action's row has `toolBonusPerTier` - Move the Body alone (config.mjs:4799-4800). CLEANUP.actions.misleadingTrail has no such field, so its threshold is `atLeastFloor(15 - 0)`, and its briefing prints the plain 15 (action-briefing.mjs:350). The GM handbook says it right (gm-handbook.en.md:1222 names the tier only for Move the Body).
findings.evidence:
config.mjs:691   hint: "Readied, it makes cleaning up easier: advantage on every clean-up roll but Move the Body, and its tier off the number to beat, never below the minimum. ..."
cleanup.mjs:1666  // Moving a body is the one Stage 6 action a Cleaning Tool helps with by
cleanup.mjs:1667  // lowering the number rather than by granting advantage - see
cleanup.mjs:1671  if (CLEANUP.toolAdvantage && tool && key !== "moveBody") calls.armSituational(1);
cleanup.mjs:1791  const relief = def.toolBonusPerTier ? cleaningTier(held) * def.toolBonusPerTier : 0;
config.mjs:4766-4773  misleadingTrail: { label: "Misleading Trail", ..., threshold: 15, ... }   // no toolBonusPerTier
player-handbook.en.md:623  A Cleaning Tool in hand does the same for a clean-up, except Move the Body, where it takes its tier off the threshold and gives no advantage.
findings.failure_scenario: A killer readies a Tier 3 cleaning kit to plant a Misleading Trail, reads the hint and the handbook as 15 - 3 = 12, rolls a 13, and the GM's card scores it a miss against 15.
findings.expected: One rule in three places: either the trail takes the tool's tier off (a `toolBonusPerTier` on its row), or the hint and the player handbook say the tier comes off the erase and reshape alone and advantage is what the tool gives a trail.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another relief on the trail's road: resolveStageSix is the only scorer of misleadingTrail and moveBody (cleanup.mjs:1719), both doors reach it (action-tamper.mjs:162, the Stage 6 panel), and its `relief` reads the row's own field; cleanupDc's tool tier serves the erase and reshape road only (resolveCleanup). The roll window and the briefing say 15, so the window and the score agree; only the item hint and the player handbook overstate. No test reads a trail scored with a tool in hand (grep of the tier files for misleading with tool or tier found none).

findings.title: Behind Closed Doors says only a successful Pick the Lock still gets a student in; Force the Door lifts the seal for everyone and a breach lifts it too
findings.what_happens: The Call's effect line, which the Monokuma reads on the tile and the table reads on the card, is "Seals a room until the time of day ends; a successful Pick the Lock still gets a student in, and those inside stay." Force the Door counts a seal among what holds the door at INFILTRATE.force.lockDc (18) and, when it gives, lifts the seal for the rest of its time of day (doors-gm.mjs:176 `liftSeal`), which opens the room to everybody; a finished Breach the Wall lifts it as well (handbook 345).
findings.failure_scenario: A Monokuma spends 2 Despair sealing the library, believing only a lockpick gets in; a student forces the door at 18 and the whole class walks in for the rest of the time of day.
findings.expected: The effect names the ways through: Pick the Lock lets one student in, Force the Door or a breach lifts the seal.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that the seal a Force lifts is the Call's seal and not a different lock: doors-gm.mjs:118-124 reads `isSealed(room)` from call-world.mjs, the same store `sealsRoom` writes. The handbooks' Despair tables say only "Seals a room for one time of day", so they are not wrong, only short.
